summary: The change fixes the root cause where it starts. Before, `Plan::build_with` built groups wave by wave by greedy joining and then derived `order` from those groups. That could place a normal item, such as `n` in the incident shape, ahead of an urgent one. Now waves set only the order (best effective priority among ready items, then rung, then age). The new `groups_in_order` builds groups from that order: an item joins the last group only when its paths are disjoint from every member and it depends on none of them. So the groups flattened always equal the order, and with one job at a time drain dispatches in plan order. I ran all four new tests and they pass: the two drain tests, which check that the urgent item starts first and that the incident shape starts u1, u2, n, u3, u4, and the two plan.rs tests, which check dependency before dependent across priority mixes, and flattened groups equalling the order with no unexplained priority inversion across build, build_capped and build_improving. Athena's recorded CI run shows fmt, clippy and tests passing. Docs in plan.rs and drain.rs, and the CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] / Fixed, describe the new behaviour. The only file outside the expected deliverables is crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. It was planned and holds only the updated group expectation the new rule requires. The other findings are small: a misplaced doc comment, and two tests that only guard against regressions.
